answers.question: I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?
answers.answer: No, don't chase the missed miles. The week you ran was already a hard week in disguise, because heat, short sleep and work stress stack on top of training load. Piling four extra miles onto this week would raise injury and burnout risk without buying real fitness. The better move is to hit every planned session clean this week, with the AC back on and sleep recovering. If this coming Sunday feels strong in the last few miles, we add distance to next Sunday's long run instead.

new.analysis:
## What happened

You followed the Tuesday easy and Saturday easy as planned, cut the Wednesday threshold to two of three reps, missed Thursday, and ended the long run at 11 of 13 miles. Given the conditions, those are reasonable in-the-moment calls, not failures. The signal I care about is the 13 bpm jump in easy heart rate at the same pace, which points at heat, sleep and stress, not lost fitness.

## Why this week looks like this

I am keeping distance close to last week's planned load rather than growing it, because you ran last week drained and short on sleep. The Wednesday session moves from threshold reps to steady marathon-pace work inside an easy run. That still trains the race system in this build phase, with less heart rate cost than 8:00/mi reps, so it is more likely to finish clean while you recover.

## The long run

Sunday goes back to 13 miles at easy effort, under 150 bpm. If it is still hot, split water at every loop or carry a bottle; stopping to drink is fine and does not count against the session. We need the time on feet to keep building toward a 2.5 to 3 hour long run over the next month.

## Life side

With the AC fixed this week, aim for 7 hours of sleep most nights; that alone will drop your easy heart rate back toward the high 130s. If the work deadline bleeds into Wednesday or the long run, tell me and we shift the quality session rather than skip it.

safetyCallouts.title: Sleep and heat load.
safetyCallouts.body: Short sleep plus heat raises heart rate, perceived effort and injury risk. If sleep stays under 6 hours and you feel drained for a second week, treat it as a reason to pull back a session, not push through. If dizziness, chest symptoms or persistent exhaustion appear, see a qualified professional.
